assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and its translation into long-acting agonists is a rare physiology-to-medicine arc: a clear mechanism (glucose-dependent insulin secretion, satiety signalling) that produced transformative therapies for diabetes and obesity with large, lasting impact on human health.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and its actions in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and intestinotrophic/therapeutic concept) and Knudsen (long-acting analogue design leading to liraglutide and semaglutide) form a coherent three-person configuration. Mojsov's structural and early peptide contribution is credited but, in my view, is the most contested; Habener is not among the supplied names, so the allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in many large randomized trials and by real-world use across several indications; the mechanism is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first established GLP-1 as the active incretin fragment and therapeutic peptide.
Drug-development contributions may be viewed by some as engineering rather than discovery.
Habener is absent from the supplied credit, limiting a fair configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial rhodopsins used as genetically targeted light-gated actuators gave neuroscience and physiology causal control of defined cell populations at millisecond resolution. The method is original, conceptually clear and has changed experimental practice across circuits, behaviour and disease models.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps were channelrhodopsin characterisation (Nagel, Bamberg, Hegemann) and the demonstration of its use in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, with Miesenböck's earlier genetically encoded light-sensitive approach). Only three names fit; Hegemann, Nagel and Deisseroth are my proposal, but Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have real claims and the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced for nearly two decades, with clinical translation (vision restoration) beginning; the tool is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit; any trio leaves out serious contributors.
It is a tool/method, with the strongest discovery component being the channelrhodopsin work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6 and related arms). It is a fundamental cell-biological discovery that connects to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter (Ire1 and the unconventional mRNA splicing mechanism and later integrated stress response work) and Mori (identification of the UPR transcriptional signalling in yeast and mammals) are the clear pair. Other contributors (Ron, Kaufman, Hendershot) exist, but the supplied credit supports a clean two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and an established conceptual framework; recognition would be mature, and therapeutic modulation is still developing.
uncertainties: Medical impact is mostly mechanistic; clinical translation remains incomplete.
Contributions of others in mammalian UPR and PERK/ISR signalling may be viewed as part of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells carrying chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new cancer therapy class. The concept is clear and the clinical impact is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T, including the early CLL responses) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early clinical immunotherapy proof of principle) give a plausible trio. Eshhar's original CAR concept and others, not in the supplied list, complicate a fair assignment.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multi-year follow-up; independent confirmation is strong, but long-term safety, durability and solid-tumour efficacy are still evolving.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR concept credit (Eshhar) is absent from the supplied names.
Prior immunotherapy recognition (checkpoint blockade) may influence timing.
Rosenberg's adoptive transfer work is related but distinct from CAR engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified cytosolic DNA as a danger signal and defined the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP, uncovering a core innate immune mechanism with implications for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunity.
assessment.attribution: Chen (identification of cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) and Barber (discovery of STING) are the two decisive contributors in my assessment; the supplied co-credits (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) were collaborators or related discoverers, and a prize naturally limits to these two.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed with a broad mechanistic literature; clinical translation (STING agonists/antagonists) has not yet delivered, so recognition could be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Chen, Barber and the supplied co-authors may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-organizing adult stem-cell-derived organoids, based on Lgr5 stem cell biology and defined niche factors, created a widely used system for modelling human tissue and disease and for personalised medicine, with strong conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader (Lgr5 stem cells and the organoid culture concept); Sato carried out the crucial first intestinal organoid culture work. A two-person prize looks plausible, though Sasai's pluripotent-cell organoid work is a separate line.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced and adopted worldwide; clinical and drug-discovery applications are still maturing, so some may regard recognition as slightly early.
uncertainties: Relationship to the stem-cell and Wnt discoveries could make the prize a compound recognition.
Clinical impact so far is limited relative to research impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of BCR-ABL with imatinib turned CML from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, an exceptional translational achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) is a defensible trio; the discovery of BCR-ABL itself (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) and chemists at Ciba-Geigy complicate a clean assignment.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of outcome data and many confirmed follow-on drugs; fully mature, with arguably a long wait already.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should recognise the oncogene discovery or the drug development.
Industry contributions and team credit at Ciba-Geigy/Novartis are hard to apportion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic modality with a mechanism-based path from RNA biology to the clinic.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanisms and identification of the target regulatory element) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a natural pair; the clinical trial leaders and others are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term outcome data and a growing family of related therapies; mature enough, though the broader oligonucleotide field is still developing.
uncertainties: Contribution of other splicing researchers and clinical investigators may be argued.
Priority between antisense approaches may be debated.
